newsitem.title: CROATIA: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - July 18.

text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian weekly Tjednik. Reuters has not verifired these stories and does not vauch for their accuracy.

- After seizing one and killing another Bosnian Serb war crimes supect, NATO artillery has deployed around central Bosnian town of Vitez and may be preparing to launch similar raid on Croat suspects there.
- Rumours fly around Bosnian Serb republic that the two war crimes suspects recently snatched by elite British NATO troops were betrayed by their close associates.

- On the eve of the first soccer match since 1991 between Croatian and Yugoslav clubs - Croatia Zagreb has support from state, politics and finances, while Partizan Belgrade has become an outsider. However, Croatia's players are under an imperative for victory. If they win they become legend, if they lose they will fall from grace of gods.

- The establishement of Serb National Council in Croatia last weekend may indicate the Serbs have given up the concept of being a constitutive nation in Croatia and are preparing to subside as a minority.
- Long-delayed meeting between Croatian president Franjo Tudjman and chairman of Bosnian collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic now seems more uncertain than ever.

- Loans - Unless international loans are used for boosting industrial production there are realistic chances that in not so distant future new loans will be used to pay off the old ones. -- Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
